description: How information flows through a health system and how software supports it: the building blocks of health systems, district health information systems such as DHIS2, facility workflows from registration to claims, indicators and routine reporting, data quality, evaluation of information systems and the history and governance of health information systems in Africa. Taught through case-based simulations of a district health directorate, with realistic reporting cycles, dashboards and data quality reviews built in browser-based tools.
modelledOn: WHO, Framework and Standards for Country Health Information Systems (Health Metrics Network)
WHO, Data Quality Review: A Toolkit for Facility Data Quality Assessment
Wager, Lee and Glaser, Health Care Information Systems: A Practical Approach for Health Care Management
Braa and Sahay, Integrated Health Information Architecture: Power to the Users
outcomes: Describe the building blocks of a health system and map the information needs of patients, clinicians, managers and policy makers at each level.
Configure a district health information system with organisation units, data elements, data sets and indicators and use it to collect and aggregate routine data.
Model health facility workflows from registration to discharge and insurance claims and identify where information is created, used and lost.
Define, calculate and interpret health indicators and produce reports and dashboards that support decisions at facility, district and national level.
Assess routine data for completeness, timeliness and consistency, and design interventions that improve data quality and use.
Evaluate a health information system against its goals using established frameworks and propose improvements suited to African health systems.

units.title: Health systems and their information needs
topics: The WHO health system building blocks; health information as one of six; universal health coverage
Levels of care in Ghana: CHPS compounds, health centres, district, regional and teaching hospitals; the Ghana Health Service
Who needs what information: patients, clinicians, facility managers, district and regional directorates, ministries, donors
Data, information, knowledge and decisions; the information cycle from collection to action
Sources of health data: routine facility data, surveys (DHS, MICS), censuses, civil registration and vital statistics, surveillance

units.title: Health information system architecture
topics: Components of a national HIS: patient-level systems, aggregate systems, registries, logistics, HR and finance systems
Paper registers, tally sheets and summary forms and how they become electronic data
Fragmentation and vertical programme systems; the case for integration and enterprise architecture
Digital health building blocks and the OpenHIE architecture in outline
Open-source platforms in common use: DHIS2, OpenMRS, OpenLMIS, iHRIS

units.title: District health information systems
topics: DHIS2 concepts: organisation unit hierarchy, data elements, category combinations, data sets, periods
Aggregate versus individual (tracker) data; programme stages and events
Data entry, offline capture on Android and synchronisation over weak networks
Aggregation, disaggregation by age and sex, and analytics tables
Configuring a district instance with facilities, monthly reports and validation rules
Ghana's national rollout of DHIS2 and lessons from other African countries

units.title: Health facility workflows
topics: Patient journeys through an outpatient department: registration, triage, consultation, laboratory, pharmacy, billing
Inpatient admission, ward management, transfer, discharge and referral between levels of care
Maternal and child health clinics, immunisation sessions and outreach by community health nurses
Health insurance workflows: NHIS membership verification, claims preparation and submission, claims auditing in Ghana
Supply chain and pharmacy stock management; stock-outs and logistics reports
Workflow modelling with BPMN and swimlane diagrams; finding duplicated recording and delays

units.title: Indicators and reporting
topics: Indicator design: numerators, denominators, targets; input, process, output, outcome and impact indicators
Population denominators and catchment areas; coverage rates for antenatal care, skilled delivery and immunisation
Programme indicators for malaria, HIV, TB and maternal health; national and SDG indicator frameworks
Reporting cycles, deadlines and feedback to facilities; avoiding reporting for its own sake
Dashboards, pivot tables, maps and scorecards for district management meetings
From data to decisions: district league tables and performance reviews

units.title: Data quality in health
topics: Dimensions of data quality: completeness, timeliness, accuracy, consistency, validity
Validation rules, outlier detection and internal consistency checks between related data elements
Data quality audits and verification: re-counting registers against reported figures; verification factors
Root causes of poor data: workload, training, form design, incentives, supervision
Improving data use: data review meetings, feedback, a culture of information use (PRISM framework)
Running a data quality review on a simulated district's monthly reports

units.title: Evaluating health information systems
topics: Why systems fail: design-reality gaps, sustainability, pilots that never scale
Evaluation frameworks: HMN assessment, PRISM, the DeLone and McLean success model
Measuring usability, adoption, data use and impact on health outcomes
Costing a health information system: total cost of ownership and sustainability planning

units.title: Health information systems in Africa
topics: History of HIS in Africa: from paper registers to DHIS2 and national digital health strategies
Governance, ownership and donor coordination; the role of ministries and health services
Infrastructure realities: power, connectivity, devices, local support and hosting
Ghana's digital health initiatives: Lightwave e-Health, the national health insurance claims system, e-Tracker
Privacy and data protection under Ghana's Data Protection Act 843 for health data

units.title: Project
topics: Assessing the information needs of a chosen district or facility
Designing data sets, indicators and dashboards to meet those needs
Planning data quality checks and a feedback cycle
Project: a configured district reporting system with a written evaluation and improvement plan
